1.1.1.3-f13.accuracy_reason: Correct: the name belonged to the dancing mania and was later used for chorea (Sydenham's chorea).

1.1.1.3-f4.accuracy_reason: The term comes from Stephen of Antioch's medieval Latin translation of Haly Abbas, rendering the Arabic umm al-dimāgh. It is still the standard anatomical term.

1.1.1.3-f7.accuracy_reason: In older medicine, coma meant a deep, morbid sleepiness, and Burton does pair it with Sopor.

1.1.1.3-f8.accuracy_reason: Coma vigil was described in this way in early modern medicine, and vigilia meant morbid sleeplessness.
